name: Wildflowers
description: A loose patch of meadow flowers. Quick to bloom, and the first thing pollinators look for.

facts.text: Flowering patches offer nectar to butterflies and bees.
Grows fastest in open, sunny ground that is neither parched nor waterlogged.
Several flowering patches together draw rarer visitors.

name: Garden moss
description: A soft green carpet that creeps across damp, shaded ground and softens old stone.

facts.text: A mature carpet slowly spreads onto neighbouring shaded grass.
Moss holds moisture, keeping the ground around it damp.

name: Fern
description: Arching fronds that fill sheltered corners with cool, layered green.

facts.text: New fronds unfurl from tightly coiled fiddleheads.
Dense fronds give ground creatures somewhere to hide.

name: Ornamental grass
description: Fine, arching blades that sway in the breeze and give the garden vertical texture.

facts.text: A mature clump offers cover to creatures moving through the garden.

name: Japanese maple
description: A slow-growing ornamental tree. In time it shades the ground and drops twigs and leaves.

facts.text: A young maple begins to cast shade on the tiles around it.
Its small spring flowers are visited by bees.
A mature maple sheds its finely cut leaves and weeps a little sweet sap.

hints.text: You carry a winged seed. Plant it early: a tree takes time.

name: Soft rush
description: Upright green stems that thrive in wet ground at the water's edge.

facts.text: Rushes soften the pond's edge and give cover to small water creatures.

name: Old black pine
description: An ancient pine, older than anyone's memory of the garden. It still sheds twigs, bark and needles.

facts.text: Its wide canopy keeps the corner beneath it cool and damp.
Black pines are a classic feature of Japanese gardens, often shaped over generations.

name: Old azalea
description: A dense, rounded shrub left from the garden's first planting. Its low branches cast a soft, dappled shade.

facts.text: Its tangle of low branches gives small creatures somewhere sheltered to rest.
Azaleas are often clipped into soft mounds in Japanese gardens, a style called o-karikomi.

name: Bamboo
description: Tall, jointed culms that whisper in the wind and cast a cool, green shade.

facts.text: Bamboo is a grass, and some kinds grow faster than any other plant.
A dense clump gives birds and small animals shelter from wind and rain.

hints.text: Something tall grows beyond the north wall.

name: Japanese forest grass
description: Soft, arching blades that flow like water across a shady floor.

facts.text: Its blades all lean one way, as if combed by the wind.
Grows happily in the dappled shade under bamboo.

hints.text: Clearing the grove's overgrowth may turn up something to plant.

name: Hosta
description: Broad, ribbed leaves that fill shady corners, with lilac flower spikes in summer.

facts.text: Bumblebees visit its tall flower spikes.
Deep shade suits it best; strong sun scorches the leaves.

hints.text: Clearing the grove's overgrowth may turn up something to plant.

name: Water lily
description: Round floating leaves and cup-shaped flowers that open in the sun.

facts.text: Its pads shade the water, keeping it cool for pond life.
Pond skaters rest on the pads between dashes across the water.

hints.text: Some plants grow out in open water, not on the bank.

name: Common reed
description: Tall feathery reeds that colonise the shallow margin.

facts.text: Dragonflies rest on the tall stems between flights.
A reed bed slowly spreads along the margin by its roots.

hints.text: Clearing the banks may turn up something that grows at the water’s edge.

name: Hornwort
description: A submerged pond plant of soft, feathery whorls.

facts.text: It keeps deep water clear and fresh.
Young pond insects shelter among its whorls.

hints.text: Something can grow wholly under water in the deepest part of the pond.

name: Map lichen
description: Yellow-green patches that creep across bare stone and gravel.

facts.text: It grows only on or beside stone.
Lichens are a sign of clean, unpolluted air.

hints.text: Something small grows on the bare gravel beside old stones.

name: Creeping thyme
description: A low, fragrant mat that flowers purple in dry, sunny spots.

facts.text: Bees crowd its tiny flowers on warm days.
It prefers poor, dry soil to rich ground.

name: Blue fescue
description: Neat tufts of fine, blue-grey grass for dry ground.

facts.text: Its tufts give small creatures cover on open ground.

name: Dwarf mountain pine
description: A slow, rounded little pine that suits stone and gravel.

facts.text: Small creatures shelter beneath its low branches.
Jumping spiders bask on its sunlit needles.

name: Old alder
description: A tall alder of the damp hollow, its roots in wet ground.

facts.text: Alders love wet ground and enrich the soil around them.
Its fallen leaves feed the woodland floor.

name: Royal fern
description: A large, stately fern of damp, shaded ground.

facts.text: One of the largest ferns, at home in damp hollows.
Its fronds shelter the woodland floor from drying out.

name: Wood sorrel
description: Clover-like leaves and delicate white flowers on the shaded floor.

facts.text: Its leaves fold up at night and in rain.

name: Oyster mushroom
description: Soft grey-brown fans that grow from rotting wood.

facts.text: It grows only beside dead wood, which it slowly breaks down.
Fungi return the wood’s goodness to the soil.

hints.text: Something grows only beside the fallen logs.

name: Turkey tail
description: Banded brackets in brown and cream, layered like a fan.

facts.text: Each bracket is banded like a turkey’s tail feathers.

name: White clover
description: Low trefoil leaves and round white flower heads.

facts.text: Bees and hoverflies visit its little flower heads.
It feeds the soil through its roots.

name: Oxeye daisy
description: Tall white daisies with sunny yellow centres.

facts.text: Its open flowers suit short-tongued visitors like hoverflies.

name: Aster
description: Starry lilac flowers that bloom late into the year.

facts.text: Late flowers keep pollinators fed when little else blooms.

name: Bellflower
description: Nodding violet bells on slender stems.

facts.text: Small bees sleep inside its bells on cool nights.

name: Meadow grass
description: Tall, swaying meadow grasses that turn golden.

facts.text: Grasshoppers sing from tall grass on warm days.
Leaving some grass long gives insects a place to shelter.

name: Japanese iris
description: Tall sword leaves and broad purple flowers at the water’s edge.

facts.text: Demoiselles rest on its tall leaves.
Irises are a classic of Japanese stream gardens.

name: Streamside sedge
description: Arching clumps of fine green leaves that hold the bank together.

facts.text: Its roots hold the stream bank firm.
Mayflies rest among its leaves.

name: Marsh fern
description: A soft fern of wet, shaded banks.

facts.text: It keeps shaded banks cool and damp.

name: Old cherry
description: A gnarled flowering cherry, the heart of the court.

facts.text: Its blossom draws the first bees of the year.
Old cherries are often propped with wooden crutches.

name: Flowering cherry
description: A young cherry tree that will cloud the court with blossom.

facts.text: Bush warblers sing from blossoming branches.

name: Camellia
description: A glossy evergreen shrub with waxy red flowers.

facts.text: White-eyes come to drink from its flowers.
Whole flowers drop to the ground, petals intact.

name: Satsuki azalea
description: A low, clipped azalea smothered in pink flowers.

facts.text: Bees crowd its open flowers.

name: Hydrangea
description: Lacecap flowers of blue and pink in dappled shade.

facts.text: Its small inner flowers feed insects; the showy outer ones do not.

name: Flowering quince
description: A spreading, thorny shrub with scarlet blossom and golden fruit.

facts.text: Its fruit is hard and sour, but birds love it.

name: Ancient konara oak
description: A vast old oak, hollowed by age, its canopy spread wide over the garden.

facts.text: An old oak supports more kinds of life than almost any other tree.
Its hollows are homes for birds, bats and dormice.

name: Japanese holly
description: A dense evergreen shrub of the understory, red-berried in winter.

facts.text: Its dense evergreen leaves shelter small birds through winter.

name: Ivy
description: Evergreen ivy, clambering over the ground and up old stumps.

facts.text: Its late flowers feed insects when little else is in bloom.

name: Wood anemone
description: White starry flowers that carpet the woodland floor.

facts.text: A carpet of anemones is a sign of very old woodland.

name: Cattail
description: Tall reed-mace with brown velvet heads, in the shallows and mud.

facts.text: Reed warblers sing from cattail and reed stems.
A dense stand shelters the marsh’s birds.

name: Marsh marigold
description: Glossy round leaves and bright golden cups at the water’s edge.

facts.text: Its early flowers feed the first insects of the year.

name: Frogbit
description: Small floating rosettes like tiny lily pads, with white flowers.

facts.text: Moorhens pick their way among its floating leaves.
Leave some water open: a marsh needs pools as well as plants.

name: Old Japanese maple
description: A broad old maple whose leaves turn scarlet in autumn.

facts.text: It drops its leaves in autumn, a carpet of red underfoot.

name: Japanese apricot
description: Ume: a small tree that blossoms pink and white in late winter.

facts.text: It flowers in late winter and early spring, feeding the first insects.
Bush warblers and ume blossom go together in Japanese poems.

name: Japanese beautyberry
description: An arching shrub that bears clusters of violet berries in autumn.

facts.text: It flowers in summer and fruits in autumn.

name: Mondo grass
description: Low tufts of dark green that stay fresh all year.

facts.text: Evergreen ground cover gives small creatures shelter in winter.

name: Snowdrop
description: Nodding white flowers in the coldest months.

facts.text: It flowers in winter, when a warm day brings out the first bees.

name: Lotus
description: Great round leaves held above the water, and pink flowers that rise from the mud.

facts.text: Dragonflies rest on its tall flower buds.
The lotus rises clean from muddy water: a symbol of purity.

hints.text: Something grand could grow in the ornamental pond.

name: Weeping cherry
description: A cherry whose branches fall like a waterfall of blossom.

facts.text: Its falling branches make a room of blossom beneath.
